# Decisions: viewer-ux-panels-lists

From the grill session of 2026-09-27 with the operator.

## Decisions

- Runs home's Recent section lists every finished run of the last 7 days across all projects, newest first, with no count cap: the `lists` lane filters on `activity.finished_at` (else `updated_at`), and `runs-home` asserts a run older than 7 days is absent from Recent while it stays on its project page.
- No client fan-out fallback: the `lists` lane reads the served `activity` only. A run without `activity` shows `<Status> · updated <time>` with no finish time, no duration and no Needs-you grouping, and nothing polls per workflow or per run to reconstruct it.
- The operator's live registry will serve run directories (`viewer.expose_run_dir` for `project-b` and `md-manager`) after this run lands: the `lists` lane only reads `run_dir`; it changes no registry file outside the test harness, and its fixtures set the key in their own temp registry.

## Assumptions

- `contracts/projects/triage.ts` (`deriveNow`) and `contracts/projects/v1.ts` are read-only for both lanes; a wording or field that seems missing is recorded in the lane's handoff as a follow-up, not added.
- Needs you lists runs whose `activity.attention.kind` is `question`, `pane` or `approval`; Running lists non-terminal runs not already in Needs you; a run appears in one section only.
- Reviewer deadlines use `inputs.automatic.review_timeout_seconds` and carry `≈`; with `launched_at` null the `panels` lane shows "launch time not recorded" and no deadline.
- Both lanes keep every existing test id; new test ids follow the PRD's names where it gives one.

## Deferred

- The one-request list endpoint (PRD B4) and the evidence detail fields (B5).
- Slice S7 (Assignment reorder, review diff inline): the separate feature `viewer-ux-depth` after this run is integrated.
- Controller and exporter follow-ups C1 to C10 of PRD section 9.4.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

557	## 5. Timeline and time display rules
558	
559	### 5.1 Model
560	
561	`contracts/projects/triage.ts` (pure, no React, shared with the server for B2) exports:
562	
563	```ts
564	buildTimeline({ definition, snapshot, events, inputs, review?, laneResults?, now }): {
565	  runStart: Instant; runEnd: Instant | null;             // runEnd = last non-controller activity, never updated_at
566	  spans: Span[];      // one per node attempt: node_id, lane, attempt, start, end, status, outcome, live
567	  markers: Marker[];  // diagnosis | repair | controller_start | controller_error | interrupted | question | answer | log
568	  gaps: Gap[];        // operator | controller_down | waiting_worker | idle, with from/to/ms
569	  byNode: Map<string, Span[]>;
570	}
571	type Instant = { at: string; source: 'event' | 'receipt' | 'check' | 'review' | 'inferred'; note?: string }
572	```
573	
574	It is memoized on `(snapshot.last_sequence, inputs identity, review identity)`, so a 5 s poll that brings nothing new does not rebuild it.
575	
576	### 5.2 Derivation rules
577	
578	Each rule carries its source tag, which the UI shows in a tooltip. Each rule has a unit test on the captured payloads.
579	
580	1. **Attempt number.** Re-read it from the message with `/\battempt (\d+)/i` before falling back to `event.attempt`. The server parser is case-sensitive (server/projects.ts:1067-1070), so every challenge event reads "attempt 1" today. Expected on skeleton-001: challenge attempts 1, 2, 3.
581	2. **Controller rows.** On any node, a message matching `^Automatic checkpoint controller PID \d+` is a `controller_start` marker, never a node status. A `^\[Errno \d+\]` failure on a node that later succeeded is a `controller_error` marker. This fixes guardrails `launch_controller` #5-#17/#24/#29/#32 until B1 lands.
582	3. **Spans.** A `running` status event opens a span for (node, attempt). The next terminal status (succeeded, failed, paused, cancelled) closes it. A new attempt that opens while the previous one is still open closes it as "ended without a record". Example: challenge attempt 1, 08:39:42 → 08:45:55.
583	4. **Receipts and evidence.** When events are missing:
584	   - A worker span runs from `native_started_at` (else `launch_requested_at`) to `stop.confirmed_at`, or to *now* while running. The source is "receipt". Example: 08:50:52 → 09:19:13 = 28m21s.
585	   - A review without events ends at `reviewed_at`. Its start is the earliest `reviewers[].launched_at`, else the end of the step it depends on, marked ≈ inferred.
586	   - A candidate without a `running` event starts ≈ at the end of the last verify step. Example: 09:29:15 → 09:30:21.
587	   - An approval without an event is ≈ an instant at the integrate event's time, with the note "no approval event recorded".
588	5. **Run-level rows** (`node_id` null):
589	   - `failed identically` becomes a **diagnosis** marker (⚑), attached to the lane named in `<phase>/<lane>`.
590	   - `^Repair (\d+) applied` becomes a **repair** marker (⚒). It carries the snapshot and files from the node's `paused` "Repair n by the operator" event (#20).
591	   - `Supervisor interrupted` / `Claude Code was unavailable` become an **interrupted** marker.
592	   - A controller row whose raw status was `blocked` becomes a **controller_blocked** marker (✗). With B1 it is served as `status: 'failed'` on a node-less row. Before B1, it is recognised as a node-less row that is not one of the running-type messages: the PID checkpoint, `^Rerunning `, `^Resuming `, `^Repair \d+ applied`. Examples: `Worker game deadline exhausted; no automatic relaunch` (automatic.py:1284), `… failed identically on attempts 1 and 2 …` (advance_or_block, :1011; this one is also the diagnosis), and `… ended on it in a state no resume continues` (:1323).
593	   - Anything else is a plain log row.
594	6. **Gaps.** A stretch of more than 120 s with no event becomes a gap row, classified by what surrounds it:

`contracts/projects/triage.ts` (pure, no React, shared with the server for B2) exports:

```ts

  runStart: Instant; runEnd: Instant | null;             // runEnd = last non-controller activity, never updated_at
  spans: Span[];      // one per node attempt: node_id, lane, attempt, start, end, status, outcome, live
  markers: Marker[];  // diagnosis | repair | controller_start | controller_error | interrupted | question | answer | log
  gaps: Gap[];        // operator | controller_down | waiting_worker | idle, with from/to/ms
  byNode: Map<string, Span[]>;
}
type Instant = { at: string; source: 'event' | 'receipt' | 'check' | 'review' | 'inferred'; note?: string }
```

It is memoized on `(snapshot.last_sequence, inputs identity, review identity)`, so a 5 s poll that brings nothing new does not rebuild it.

### 5.2 Derivation rules

Each rule carries its source tag, which the UI shows in a tooltip. Each rule has a unit test on the captured payloads.

2. **Controller rows.** On any node, a message matching `^Automatic checkpoint controller PID \d+` is a `controller_start` marker, never a node status. 4. **Receipts and evidence.** When events are missing:

   - A candidate without a `running` event starts ≈ at the end of the last verify step. Example: 09:29:15 → 09:30:21.

   - inside a worker span with no other cause: **worker working**. Example: 28m21s.
   - otherwise: **no activity**.

1	/**
2	 * The fixture extension point of the viewer UX slices (docs/PRD_VIEWER_UX.md section 11). Each slice adds its runs in its
3	 * own module, `ux-<slice>.ts`, as a new workflow `ux-<slice>` appended after every workflow of `PROJECT`, so the existing
4	 * counts (two projects, five runs in `feature-flow`) do not change:
5	 * - `payloads`: the contract payloads the worker-phase mocks serve. This module spreads them into the maps `fixtures.ts`
6	 *   exports when it is first imported; `mock.ts` imports it, so they are merged before any request is served.
7	 * - `seed`: writes the same logical runs for the candidate phase and returns their registry entries; `seedCandidate`
8	 *   calls every module's seed with a `SeedContext`, appends the entries to `PROJECT`'s workflows and adds any top-level
9	 *   registry keys a module returns (S6's `viewer.expose_run_dir`, once the server accepts it).
10	 * After S1 no slice edits `fixtures.ts`, `mock.ts` or `seed.ts`: a slice changes only its own module. Modules import the
11	 * builders `fixtures.ts` exports and only types from here and from `seed.ts`, so no import cycle exists.
12	 */
13	import type { ReviewResult, RunDetail, RunInputs, WorkflowDefinition } from '../../../contracts/projects/v1.ts'
14	import type { WorkerResult, WorkflowEvent } from '../../../contracts/workflow/v1.ts'
15	import {
16	  artifactFiles, PROJECT, reviewResults, runDetails, runEvents, runInputs, runLists, workerResults, workflowLists,
17	  type ArtifactFile, type DefinitionNode,
18	} from '../fixtures.ts'
19	import type { SeedContext } from '../seed.ts'
20	import { uxLaunch } from './ux-launch.ts'
21	import { uxLists } from './ux-lists.ts'
22	import { uxNode } from './ux-node.ts'
23	import { uxReview } from './ux-review.ts'
24	import { uxRun } from './ux-run.ts'
25	import { uxTime } from './ux-time.ts'
26	import { uxVerify } from './ux-verify.ts'
27	
28	/** A module's worker-phase payloads, keyed like the maps of `fixtures.ts`; run lists are derived from `runDetails`. */
29	export type UxPayloads = {
30	  /** Registered after every existing workflow of `PROJECT`, in module order. */
31	  workflows: WorkflowDefinition[]
32	  runDetails: Record<string, RunDetail>
33	  runEvents: Record<string, WorkflowEvent[]>
34	  /** Per run, keyed `<node>/<attempt>` or `candidate_<lane>/<attempt>` like the results route. */
35	  workerResults: Record<string, Record<string, WorkerResult>>
36	  reviewResults: Record<string, ReviewResult>
37	  runInputs: Record<string, RunInputs>
38	  artifactFiles: Record<string, ArtifactFile[]>
39	}
40	
41	/** One registry workflow entry, as `seedCandidate` writes them. */
42	export type RegistryWorkflow = { workflow_id: string; runs_root: string; definition: { name: string; nodes: DefinitionNode[] } }
43	
44	/** What a module's candidate-phase seed adds to the registry. */
45	export type UxSeed = {
46	  workflows: RegistryWorkflow[]
47	  /** Top-level registry keys beside `version` and `projects`; a later module's key replaces an earlier one's. */
48	  registry?: Record<string, unknown>
49	}
50	
51	export type UxFixtureModule = {
52	  payloads?: Partial<UxPayloads>
53	  seed?: (context: SeedContext) => UxSeed
54	}
55	
56	/** In slice order; the order the added workflows are listed in, in both phases. */
57	export const UX_FIXTURE_MODULES: readonly UxFixtureModule[] = [uxTime, uxRun, uxNode, uxVerify, uxLaunch, uxReview, uxLists]
58	
59	function mergePayloads(modules: readonly UxFixtureModule[]) {
60	  for (const { payloads = {} } of modules) {
61	    const workflows = payloads.workflows ?? []
62	    workflowLists[PROJECT.project_id].workflows.push(...workflows)
63	    Object.assign(runDetails, payloads.runDetails)
64	    Object.assign(runEvents, payloads.runEvents)
65	    Object.assign(workerResults, payloads.workerResults)
66	    Object.assign(reviewResults, payloads.reviewResults)
67	    Object.assign(runInputs, payloads.runInputs)
68	    Object.assign(artifactFiles, payloads.artifactFiles)
69	    // The mocks index these per run: a run without events, results or artifacts serves none rather than failing.
70	    for (const runId of Object.keys(payloads.runDetails ?? {})) {
71	      runEvents[runId] ??= []
72	      workerResults[runId] ??= {}
73	      artifactFiles[runId] ??= []
74	    }
75	    // Each workflow's runs sorted by `updated_at` descending then `run_id` ascending, as the contract requires.
76	    for (const workflow of workflows) {
77	      runLists[workflow.workflow_id] = {
78	        runs: Object.values(runDetails).map(detail => detail.summary).filter(summary => summary.workflow_id === workflow.workflow_id)
79	          .sort((a, b) => b.updated_at.localeCompare(a.updated_at) || a.run_id.localeCompare(b.run_id)),
80	        next_cursor: null,
81	      }
82	    }
83	  }
84	}
85	
86	mergePayloads(UX_FIXTURE_MODULES)
87	
88	/** Seeds every module's runs for the candidate phase; returns what to add to the registry, in module order. */
89	export function seedUxFixtures(context: SeedContext): Required<UxSeed> {
90	  const seeded = UX_FIXTURE_MODULES.map(module => module.seed?.(context) ?? { workflows: [] })
91	  return {
92	    workflows: seeded.flatMap(seed => seed.workflows),
93	    registry: Object.assign({}, ...seeded.map(seed => seed.registry ?? {})) as Record<string, unknown>,
94	  }
95	}

concerns.message: The panels lane doesn't own src/projects/NodeDetail.tsx, and that file decides what data each section component gets. ControllerSections receives only `scope` and `renderResult` (NodeDetail.tsx:260, ControllerSections.tsx:28). It gets no inputs, events, timeline, node or clock. ChallengeSections receives only `inputs` (NodeDetail.tsx:245). ReviewSections gets inputs and node but no timeline or clock. Yet the controller-panels scenario needs: the handoff wait (`inputs.workers[].receipt.native_started_at`/`launch_requested_at` → freeze or `stop.confirmed_at`), the approval `≈` instant (the integrate event's time, from events/timeline), and the branch and commit that integrate fast-forwarded (events or `inputs.source_branch`). The challenge headline's `11m07s over 3 attempts` needs the first attempt's start, which is in the timeline, not in `inputs.challenge` (that has only attempt, attempts and decided_at). The PRD's section index chips (`[Blocking 1] [Findings 4]`, `[Concerns 8] [Alternative & experiment]`) are built in NodeDetail's `sections` array (lines 170-179), which the lane also can't edit.
concerns.consequence: The worker has three ways out and all are bad. (1) It edits NodeDetail.tsx, and the verifier's ownership check rejects the snapshot. (2) It calls fetchEvents, fetchRunInputs, buildTimeline and useNow a second time inside the section components. That duplicates RunView's polling, ignores refreshToken and breaks the 'one useNow at RunView' rule (PRD 5.3), which is rework for S7. (3) It stops at `blocked` because controller-panels can't be met. Either way the lane is likely to need a rework round.

concerns.message: Both lanes' fixtures are added to PROJECT through fixtures/index.ts, so in the combined candidate Runs home lists the panels lane's runs too. The manual run awaiting approval (attention `approval`) lands in Needs you, and the running native review lands in Running. The lists lane writes runs-home in a worktree where ux-review.ts is still empty. Any assertion there on section counts (`Needs you · N`, `Running · N`, 'nothing is running') or on the exact contents of Recent passes in the lists snapshot and fails on the combined candidate. The same is true of lists changes to the CommandBlock/NowBanner DOM that the panels tests' node-next command assertions read.
concerns.consequence: The combined candidate check fails after both workers finish, and one lane needs another attempt. To avoid it: the lists lane scopes runs-home assertions to its own run ids (never whole-section counts), and the panels lane asserts command text with toContainText on `node-next`, not on CommandBlock's internal structure.
